hypothesis: The best config already runs 3 calls (inspect starter plus Read design.png, one big write+build+smoke, final summary), at about 64k tokens, and each call re-reads 15-24k of context. The first call is pure exploration: the starter is identical every run, and the inline spec already carries the design tokens and layout notes. If the system prompt states the starter facts in prose and tells the agent to skip inspection and the design image, the first call is gone. Writing everything at once then costs 2 calls plus the final reply. That removes about one call of 15-18k cache-read tokens, plus the ~1.4k image carried across later calls, plus the ~0.5k inspect output.
changeSummary: Rewrote system-prompt.md only. It now describes the fixed starter layout in prose: ESM package with build/start scripts, a placeholder Express backend, a final index.html, and a placeholder main.jsx. It then tells the agent to skip exploration and not view /spec/design.png. The first call is one Bash that writes every file, builds, smoke-tests the API on a spare port with a temp DB and prints only failures. A fix call happens only if that fails, followed by a summary of at most 3 sentences. It also adds one quality note on keyboard focus and Tab order when a row enters edit mode, because exp-0008 failed ui.keyboard. config.json is unchanged (tools Bash/Read/Edit/Write, append mode).

 - There is no network access. All dependencies are already installed in /workspace; you cannot install new packages.
-- The specification is in /spec (read-only). The reference design images are /spec/design.png and /spec/design-mobile.png.
-- Before finishing, run `npm run build` and smoke-test the app: start it in the background on a spare port with a temporary DATABASE_PATH, exercise the API with a small Node script using fetch (curl is not installed), including error cases, check that `/` serves the built frontend, then stop the server.
-- When everything builds and works, stop and reply with a short summary.
+- The specification (requirements, API contract, design tokens) is already in your prompt; do not re-read it from /spec.
+- Every model call re-sends the whole conversation, so the number of calls is what costs. Target exactly 2 calls plus the final reply. Do NOT explore first.
+
+Known starter layout (do not inspect it, it is already known):
+- /workspace/package.json is ESM ("type": "module") with scripts `build` (vite build with frontend/vite.config.js) and `start` (node backend/server.js). Dependencies present: express 5, better-sqlite3, react 19, react-dom, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, @fontsource/inter. Do not touch package.json or the vite config; they already build frontend/ into frontend/dist.
+- backend/server.js is a placeholder Express app: it reads PORT, answers /api with 501, serves frontend/dist statically with an index.html fallback. Overwrite it completely.
+- frontend/index.html is final and loads /src/main.jsx. frontend/src/main.jsx is a placeholder that renders a stub App; overwrite it and add your own component and CSS files under frontend/src.
+
+Workflow:
+1. First call: ONE Bash command that creates every file (backend + frontend, via heredocs, whole files, no placeholders), then runs `npm run build`, starts the server in the background on a spare port with a temporary DATABASE_PATH, runs a small Node fetch script (curl is missing) exercising every endpoint including validation and 404 error cases and checking that `/` serves HTML, kills the server, and prints only failures plus a one-line OK summary (pipe the build through tail -n 5). Do not view /spec/design.png: the design tokens and layout notes in the prompt are enough.
+2. Only if that output shows a problem, fix it with one targeted command that also re-runs the checks.
+3. Then reply with a summary of at most 3 sentences.
+
+Quality notes, since there is no second chance to look at the result: use exactly the accessible names, roles, labels and texts from the spec; keep a logical DOM and Tab order; when a row enters edit mode, move focus to its "Edit title" input programmatically so it is reachable by keyboard; Escape cancels and Enter saves; follow the design tokens for spacing, colors and responsive layout at desktop and mobile widths.
evidence: Run run-20261115-121556-022c36 (63.7k, 3 calls): call 1 was `cat package.json; find ...; cat backend/*.js; cat frontend/index.html vite.config` plus Read /spec/design.png. It had 167 output tokens, 537 tokens of text output and a 1.37k image. The context was 15.2k at that point. Call 2 wrote everything in one 13k-char heredoc Bash with build and smoke, and its context was 17.7k. Call 3 was the summary at 24.4k context. The same three-call shape appears in runs fcbbc8, 8f63ad and 21ac9c (~64.6k each). The 4-call run ddbd47 (82.9k) had a failed first Bash (exit 1), then a second cat, which shows exploration is fragile and costs a full call. The README notes one run never viewed design.png and still scored visual 100. The starter files, which I read in /workspace, are what the new prompt now describes. Replacing the system prompt (exp-0008, exp-0009) saved little against noise and caused a ui.keyboard failure, so this change keeps append mode and only removes a call.
expectedSavings: Dropping call 1 removes about 15.2k of cache-read context. The image and inspect output (~1.9k) are no longer carried over the later two calls, which saves about 3.8k. Call 2's context becomes about 15k instead of 17.7k, and the new prompt adds about 0.4k per call. Estimated total is about 64.7k → about 46-50k, or roughly 15-18k (25%) per run. Risks: (1) a blind first write may break the build, which costs one extra call and brings the run back to about 64k; (2) skipping design.png could lower the visual score, though the inline design tokens and requirements layout notes should keep it ≥95; (3) a blind keyboard or accessibility miss. The quality notes in the prompt are there to cover (3).
